newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan sentences 47 people for selling secrets.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan sentences 47 people for selling secrets.

text.p: A Taiwan court has sentenced 47 people including 26 government officials to prison terms of up to seven years and four months for selling information about private individuals, the China Times newspaper said on Sunday.
The paper said the central Taichung District Court handed down the verdicts on Saturday after a year-long trial.
It said the 26 government officials colluded with 21 private inquiry agency operators, who are like private detectives, to obtain information about Taiwanese residents.
Most of the cases occured in Taichung, the paper said.
Officials were not available for comment on the verdicts, which ranged from three months to seven years and four months. All 47 offenders were tried at the same time.
The convicted officials came from the police and prisons departments and government agencies involved in construction, labour insurance, tax, land administration and finance.
The officials sold data about census returns, real estate and business registration, motor vehicle registry and property registration and bugged telephone calls, the paper said.
They received between T$300 (US$11) and T$1,500 for each piece of information, the paper said.
"It's urgent to regulate the private inquiry agencies as such a condition is wide-spread now," the paper added. ($1= T$27.5)
